title: Replay, rebuild, and explain the complete event system
outcome: Design a safe projection rebuild and explain which effects may and may not be replayed.
benefits: Makes replay a controlled engineering operation.
drawbacks: Missing history, privacy, and irreversible effects can limit recovery.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes
cue: Replay the facts for a purpose, not every side effect.

trace.title: Rebuild purpose
trace.detail: Replay is a tool for a purpose. Rebuilding a reporting projection from retained facts can be useful. Re-sending every email or charging every payment again is a different and often unacceptable effect. Separate rebuildable projections from irreversible side-effect workflows.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Choose rebuild purpose → validate retained/backfill source → create isolated projection identity → replay → compare to authority/expected fixtures → switch reads → monitor → retire old state under retention policy.

For restore, draw the timeline of DB state, outbox marks, Kafka retained records, group commits, and inbox/projection state. Recovery is a reconciliation problem across those boundaries.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Resetting offsets while keeping the same inbox can result in no new projection writes. Clearing inbox blindly can repeat external effects. Old events may contain data that current privacy policy no longer permits retaining/replaying.
